Marissa — draft inventory below (summary) and I've uploaded the detailed spreadsheet (DPA_subprocessor_list_v1.xlsx). High level:

1) TelemetryCo — Observability/metrics (processing: ingestion + retention for 30 days). Primary processing: Ireland (EU); backup ingestion to US for analytics (flag: EU->US).
2) EdgeCache Ltd — CDN/edge caching (processing: caching and content routing). Primary processing: Singapore (APAC); edge nodes may touch EU for some customers (flag: EU->APAC).
3) SFTP-Integrator — temporary onboarding access for logs (processing: file transfer only). EU-hosted; no exports except SFTP session to FinServ SFTP endpoint (flag: controlled).
4) KMS Provider (Redwood-managed HSM) — key wrapping/e2e encryption metadata (no plaintext). For FinServ we can offer customer-managed keys via their KMS partner (note: there is an integration lead time).
5) AnalyticsPartner — rerank/embeddings pipeline (USA) — will need a canary model with privacy filters (flag: EU->US).

Open items:
- EdgeCache in SG: need confirmation if FinServ requires strict EU-only residency — we can route traffic to EU POPs but can't guarantee 100% (workload dependent).
- TelemetryCo: we can enable EU-only retention and aggregate telemetry; US export is optional and can be switched off for this account.

Attachments: DPA_subprocessor_list_v1.xlsx, kms_hsm_inventory.pdf, export_controls_matrix.csv (stubs)

If Proc asks for temporary access windows, propose: 2026-11-06 -> 2026-11-20, limited scopes (SFTP read-only, console support via recorded sessions).

Kimberly Park

- Telemetry data can be pseudonymized at ingestion (hashing + tokenization) and routed to EU-only telemetry cluster for this tenant. That removes most EU->US exposure.
- For EdgeCache: we can pin origin to EU POPs and disable SG POPs for FinServ beta, but performance trade-offs may occur.
- Temporary access: recommend short-lived S3/SFTP credentials (48-72h) and session recordings for console support.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration (requires 2-week lead time and an onboarding ticket).

I'll prepare the ops bullet list for the consolidated response.

Hi Suresh — thanks for the note. Attached is a consolidated package for DPA review (DPA_subprocessor_list_v1.xlsx + export_controls_matrix.csv + kms_hsm_inventory.pdf). Key points up front:

1) Subprocessors (summary rows): TelemetryCo (IE) — flag EU->US (optional, disableable); EdgeCache Ltd (SG) — flag EU->APAC (we can route EU-only POPs for beta); SFTP-Integrator (EU) — limited scope; AnalyticsPartner (US) — EU->US.
2) KMS model: Redwood provides a default Redwood-managed HSM. For FinServ we propose customer-managed keys (CMK) via their KMS — we can enable this but it's an integration item (approx. 2 weeks).
3) Proposed temporary access window (onboarding): 2026-11-06T00:00Z -> 2026-11-20T23:59Z. Scope: read-only SFTP for onboarding logs, 48-72h short-lived support credentials, recorded console sessions.
4) Mitigations: EU-only telemetry toggle (ops can enable), pseudonymization at ingestion, retention caps (30 days default for telemetry), onshore fallback routing if FinServ needs EU-only residency enforced.

Next steps we propose:
- Confirm that the proposed window is acceptable and whether you need EU-only enforcement for TelemetryCo & AnalyticsPartner.
- If CMK is required, notify us ASAP so we can start integration (2-week lead).
- We can sign a limited addendum to the DPA that enumerates the temporary access window and the specific subprocessors for the pilot.

DocuSign link for the addendum: https://docusign.com/s/REDWOOD-FIN-TRIAL-202611 (stub).

If you want, we can schedule a quick 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the package with Procurement & Legal.

Regards,
